title: Buttermilk Waffles
description: Crisp-edged, fluffy buttermilk waffles with a light batter that’s mixed in minutes. Freeze extras and toast them for busy mornings.

image.alt: A stack of waffles with butter, berries and syrup

ingredients.scaleNote: Only a thin coat is brushed on between waffles, whatever the batch size.

steps.text: Heat the waffle iron. Heat the oven to {temp 200F oven} and set a wire rack on a baking sheet inside to keep waffles crisp.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl whisk the buttermilk, eggs, melted butter and vanilla. Pour into the flour mixture and stir until just combined; a few lumps are fine. Let the batter rest for {time 5 min}.
Brush the iron lightly with oil. Pour in enough batter to cover about two-thirds of the grid (it spreads) and close the lid.
Cook until the waffle is deep golden and the steam slows to a trickle, usually {time 4-5 min} depending on your iron. Move it to the rack in the oven and repeat with the rest of the batter.

notes: Don’t stack hot waffles; they steam each other soft. The rack keeps them crisp.
Freeze cooled waffles in a single layer, then bag them. Reheat straight from frozen in a toaster.
